name: @keyhole/desktop
//author: Becomes CompanyName in the .exe's version resource. Without it electron-builder leaves Electron's default, and the binary claims to come from GitHub, Inc. — false attribution on an unsigned password manager is worse than a blank field.
author: Keyhole

scripts.start: npm run build --workspace @keyhole/app && npm run stage && electron .
scripts.build: npm run build --workspace @keyhole/app && npm run stage && electron-builder --win portable
scripts.//test: The main process is covered by `typecheck` (checkJs against Electron's own types) plus the manual checklist in README.md; driving a real Electron window in CI is out of scope for v1.
scripts.test: node -e "console.log('@keyhole/desktop: no unit tests (see typecheck + manual checklist)')"

//devDependencies: Exact pins, matching every other workspace. A floating range on the toolchain that produces a signed-by-nobody password-manager binary is a supply-chain hole: `npm install` on a fresh machine could pull a different builder than the one this .exe was verified with.
